questions.q: What is a SOC 2 report, precisely?
options: A single pass/fail certificate, identical in format to ISO 27001
A government-issued license required to operate a SaaS business
An internal company document with no independent auditor involved
An independent auditor's attestation on whether a service organization's controls meet chosen Trust Services Criteria, not a pass/fail certificate
questions.explain: SOC 2 produces an attestation report expressing an auditor's opinion, rather than a simple certified/not-certified badge like ISO 27001's certificate.

questions.q: What is the difference between a SOC 2 Type I and a SOC 2 Type II report?
options: Type I reviews control design at a point in time; Type II tests whether controls operated effectively over a review period, typically six to twelve months
There is no real difference between the two report types
Type II is a faster, cheaper version of Type I with less rigor
Type I covers Confidentiality only; Type II covers Availability only
questions.explain: Type I is a point-in-time design review; Type II tests whether those controls actually operated effectively over months, which is why enterprise buyers usually ask for Type II.

questions.q: Of the five SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria, which one is mandatory in every SOC 2 report?
options: Security
Privacy
Processing Integrity
Availability
questions.explain: Security is the only mandatory criterion; the other four (Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, Privacy) are scoped in based on what the organization actually does.

questions.q: What does ISO 27001 certify, as applied to a cloud environment?
options: That an organization has never experienced a data breach
That a cloud provider, rather than the customer, manages all security controls
That a specific cloud virtual machine has no security vulnerabilities
That an organization's Information Security Management System (ISMS), scoped to include its cloud accounts and workloads, meets the standard's requirements
questions.explain: ISO 27001 certifies an organization's ISMS — its ongoing process for managing information security risk — scoped to explicitly include the cloud environment it covers.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the real relationship between the technical controls taught earlier in this course and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 compliance work?
options: Only ISO 27001, not SOC 2, cares about access control or encryption
Compliance requires an entirely separate set of controls unrelated to IAM, logging, or encryption
SOC 2 and ISO 27001 only evaluate written policy documents, never technical configuration
Those same controls (IAM/MFA, log retention, encryption at rest) become the actual evidence for both frameworks — compliance work is mostly documenting controls already built
questions.explain: IAM and MFA, log retention, and encryption at rest each double as evidence for both SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 control areas — the controls already exist, they just get documented and produced.
